summary: Use structured slog events for production library diagnostics; package main may print command output.
Use the caller's context for production operations; use context.Background at a process entry point.
Give an exported function comment an introduction, a separate explanation, and an example or layout. This rule checks structure; review must establish that the content is accurate and useful.
Handle a panic inside each launched goroutine with a deferred recovery function.
Read peer information from the incoming context when a gRPC server method logs a request.
At a configured gRPC method-name target, use the generated _FullMethodName constant; this example requires -grpc_method_name_literal.targets=example.com/help-example.Route:0.
Log a summary after a loop instead of an info event for every iteration.
Release the underlying resource in a Close(reason string) error lifecycle method.
Return a downstream close error instead of discarding it and reporting successful lifecycle shutdown.
Emit a structured log event in functions that handle requests or change external state.
Use a concrete data type instead of any or an empty interface in production code.
Resolve the home directory explicitly because Go filesystem functions do not expand a tilde.
Fix a production finding instead of suppressing it with a nolint comment.
Return an error from library code; let main or init decide whether to exit.
Return an error for an invalid production input instead of panicking.
Log useful fields directly instead of constructing a marker-only value solely for a log event.
Remove synthetic method calls added only to defeat deadcode analysis; use method results for real behavior.
Return, store, or serve a server after registering its services instead of discarding it.
Log an operation result or a safe identifier instead of a password, token, or other secret.
Check a deferred Close error or explicitly discard it inside a deferred function.
Include the error value in error-level structured logs.
Declare a named string type and constants for a switch with a fixed set of string values.
Assert on the result of a production call; calling the function without checking an outcome cannot fail the test.
Run the real implementation of a same-module interface instead of a type declared only for tests.
Declare an external test package and test the exported API instead of calling unexported production functions.
Test the production function instead of replacing a package-level function variable or single-valued function field.
Assert on production behavior instead of reading source text to check how the function is written.
Call an error constructor directly instead of adding a function that only forwards its parameters.
Read wall-clock time in internal/clock, main, or tests; pass the time into other packages.
Use a timer and the caller's context for a cancellable delay in library code.
Log an external operation error in the function that returns its wrapped error.
